cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz, who saw the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1), is telling this one himself. It's the year King Uzziah of Judah died (2 Chronicles 26:1). And Isaiah says he saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted.

cards.question: Isaiah sees the Lord on a high, exalted throne. What fills the temple?

cards.text: Above Him stand seraphim, and each one has six wings. SIX WINGS, friend. I've got one mustache and I thought I was the most equipped guy in the room.

cards.question: Each seraph above the throne uses all six of its wings for flying.

cards.text: Two wings cover their faces, two cover their feet, and two do the flying. And the seraphim are calling out to one another about the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The seraphim above the throne are calling out to one another. What do they call out about the LORD of Hosts?

cards.text: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory." Three times, friend. Say it once and I listen. Say it THREE times and I put the dough DOWN.

cards.question: At the sound of the seraphim's voices, the temple's doorposts and thresholds stay perfectly still.
As the doorposts and thresholds shake, the temple is filled with ___.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says, "Woe is me, for I am ruined," because his eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts. I get it, friend: an important guest walks into my bakery and suddenly I see EVERY crumb on my apron.

cards.question: Standing before the King, what does Isaiah say about himself?

answers.text: He is a man of unclean lips
He is a man of slow speech
He is the least in his father's house

cards.question: Isaiah says he is the only one with unclean lips, and his people are just fine.

cards.text: Then one of the seraphim flies to Isaiah, holding a glowing coal from the altar. He took it with tongs, and friend, I respect ANYBODY who reaches for the tongs.

cards.question: With the glowing coal from the altar, the seraph touches Isaiah's ___.
After the coal touches Isaiah, what does the seraph tell him?

cards.text: The seraph says, "Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for." One touch, and the man who just said "I am ruined" hears that his sin is atoned for.
Then Isaiah hears the voice of the Lord: "Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?" That's the kind of question where a whole room suddenly gets REAL interested in the floor.

cards.question: The Lord asks whom He should send. How does Isaiah answer?

answers.text: He asks Him to send someone else

cards.text: The Lord replies with Isaiah's message, and I'll be honest, friend, this one's heavy. Go and tell this people to be ever hearing and ever seeing.

cards.question: In the Lord's message, this people keeps hearing and keeps seeing. What do they never do?

cards.text: It gets heavier, friend. The Lord says, "Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes." Hearts, ears AND eyes.

cards.question: The Lord says that otherwise the people might see, hear and understand with their hearts. Then what might they do?

cards.text: Isaiah asks, "How long, O Lord?" Friend, I asked the dust in that junk drawer the same question every single day.

cards.question: When Isaiah asks how long, the Lord says only until the next king takes the throne.
Isaiah asks the Lord how long. The Lord answers until the cities lie ruined, and until the houses are left ___.

cards.text: And He's not done answering: "until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken." Friend, I know what forsaken feels like in the back of a drawer. This is a whole LAND.

cards.question: The Lord says that though a tenth remains in the land, that tenth will be spared from any more burning.

cards.text: Then the Lord gives a picture you can SEE, friend. Buttercup would love this one: terebinth and oak trees, felled.

cards.question: The Lord says the holy seed will be in the land like what felled terebinths and oaks leave behind. What is it?

cards.text: The holy seed will be a stump in the land: cut down, but still in the ground. Friend, I spent years worn down in the back of a drawer, and I'm here to tell you, STILL THERE counts for something.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about the seraphim, 'SIX WINGS, friend,' and the mustache joke. Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card runs to four sentences: the quoted call, 'Three times, friend,' and the two sentences about saying it once and three times.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards gives the baker a basis for choosing smoke over light or music. The shaking doorposts do not imply smoke, so this blank asks for unseen wording from verse 4 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
